title: Physical Education Resources & Standards
before:
Quality pre-kindergarten through diploma physical education provides students with the skills and knowledge needed to support lifetime participation in a variety of physical activities that contribute to an active lifestyle. Physical education provides building blocks for motor skill development and analysis, physical fitness, stress reduction, decision-making, and positive social skills. 

Standards Documents

The Maine Learning Results Physical Education Standards encourage physical literacy: the ability to move with competence and confidence in a wide variety of physical activities that benefit the development of the whole child.

Adapted Physical Education (APE)

Adapted physical education (APE) is a comprehensive service delivery system established to ensure that children with a disability or identified needs has an appropriate physical education program. You will find critical information here regarding how to address student challenges connected to the psychomotor domain.

  • Maine APE Endorsement: 515
  • Adapted Physical Education National Standards
  • APE Resources

  • National Consortium for Physical Education for Individuals with Disabilities Guidance Document for Administrators

  • Maine AHPERD APE Committee

notes: Heading levels skip: jumps h1 to h5. Needs a person.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 11 links on this page open a file — 10 PDF, 1 Video — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Put the card titles on one level
decisions.why: 4 card titles are written at a level copied from an example rather than chosen — h5 on a page whose sections are h2. Only the number changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 1 list item opens with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Set a job title the way the rest of the site does
decisions.why: 1 job title sits in plain text under the person's name, where 186 elsewhere on the site are in italics — so the same contact block is drawn two ways depending on the page, and the title runs into the name above it. The standard here is the site's own, not a preference: two thirds of these blocks already do it. No word changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
